gen-comfortaa-gf-mate: Comfortaa draws round, ring-like letters with walls that never swell or thin. Mate, a text serif, brings a light stroke modulation and cupped curves, so it handles the dignified reading the heading leaves alone.
gen-comfortaa-ibm-plex-serif: IBM Plex Serif has an authoritative, corporate bearing and slimmer horizontals. Comfortaa rounds off the top with one unbroken stroke width, friendly where the body font is gently varied and sober.
gen-comfortaa-montserrat: Montserrat gives each curve generous white space and oversized e and a counters, so the lines glide like wire. Comfortaa sits a little shorter in the lowercase, which makes a long page feel unhurried.
gen-comfortaa-source-serif-4: Soft geometry up top, scholarly grain below. Comfortaa keeps its stroke edges parallel through every curve, and Source Serif 4 adds a mild stress in the o and e that rewards close reading.
gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-fira-sans: Aaargh hits hard, with a generous entry into the e's eye and bowls drawn at the same weight as the stems. Fira Sans follows with a taller x-height and wide-open s curves, professional and clean beneath the heading's muscle.
gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-karma: Heavy, confident lettering with a wide-open e. Karma, a text serif, sits close to its cap height with a quiet modulation, trustworthy and classic against the heading's bluntness.
gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-nunito: Aaargh stamps out bold letters with no thicker or thinner strokes, while its lowercase stands moderately tall. Nunito's big round bowls make a long read feel friendly.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-kiwi-maru: Kiwi Maru reads traditional and spacious, its terminals stopping well away from the stem. Its generous letterspace and ring-like o give the heavy display heading a counterpart that feels editorial.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-mate-sc: Aaargh is all commanding strokes with no hairlines and no heavy swells. But Mate SC, a classic serif, carries a faint nib-pressure variation, medium in contrast and without sharp hairlines.
gen-dafont-aaargh-plus-jakarta-sans: Plus Jakarta Sans builds every letter from a monoline stroke and keeps its curve endings well apart, a modern, precise body for the commanding Aaargh heading. Long text would flow smoothly.
